title: GABAergic neuron fate specification and lineage allocation: from development to disorder.
abstract: Review of how cis-regulatory elements (CREs) and the transcription factors binding them form gene regulatory networks that specify telencephalic inhibitory (GABAergic) neuron identity. Many disorder-associated genetic variants act at CREs or alter their regulatory activity. Argues that mapping risk-gene expression onto adult cell taxonomies often fails to reveal circuit dysfunction, and synthesizes evidence for a model in which genetic variation modulates developmental timing, fate bias and lineage allocation, producing imbalanced interneuron subtype proportions among otherwise normal cell types.
